source_snapshot.title: feat(llm): implement --format llm for the five commands that faked it
source_snapshot.body:
## What

`explain`, `read`, `status`, `doctor` and `savings` advertised `text|json|llm` and rendered `text` when given `llm`. `docs/llm-format.md` documented that fallback as intentional — commands whose output is prose or verbatim source route to "the most compact existing form".

That holds for the *payload* and not for what surrounds it. `explain`'s prose is a rendering of `facts` + `role` + `importance`, so an agent can have the inputs and skip the paragraph. `read`'s source was arriving under a 4-column line-number gutter and two ANSI escapes per line. And `explain` is the first call most plugins make on any question, so the fallback was costing the most tokens on the hottest path.

## Measured

Against `--format json`, which the help text sent agents to as the workaround:

| command | json | llm | saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| explain | 1849 | 829 | **55%** |
| doctor | 682 | 470 | 31% |
| savings --detail | 1010 | 693 | 31% |
| read (40 lines) | 1661 | 1585 | 5% |
| status | 184 | 186 | −1% |

`read` gains 23% against `text` instead — 601 of those bytes are gutter and ANSI on a 40-line read.

**`status` is a wash on size and is in anyway**, for the explicit `stale=true|false` field: that is the question the command gets called to answer, and `text` only implied it through a warning line. Its unreachable-backend path now emits the spec's `error code=...` record so a consumer parses the failure the same way it parses a result.

## Notes

- **`read`'s content block is the one place the one-record-per-line invariant is relaxed.** The preceding `content lines=<n>` record makes the block self-delimiting, so a line of source can never be mistaken for a record.
- Still on text, now documented rather than silent: `diff --content` (verbatim hunks) and `ingest` (hidden implementation-detail command).
- Found while writing this: the `doctor` status ternary. A warning there is `{ok: false, warn: true}`, so checking `warn` on the `ok` branch reports every warning as a hard failure — the opposite of what `hasFailure` concludes two lines down. Caught by the test, fixed before it shipped.

## CLAUDE.md

The paragraph on this was wrong in both directions: it claimed the deprecated `query` advertises `llm` (it offers only `text|json`) and missed `doctor`, `savings` and `ingest`. It also never mentioned that `config`, `init`, `reset`, `upgrade`, `view`, `watch` and `docker` take no `--format` at all — `--format llm` there is an `unknown option` error, not a fallback, which is the one case where an agent following the doc's "pass it unconditionally" advice breaks.

That paragraph sits between the `IX-MEMORY` markers, which say not to hand-edit. **There is no generator for it in this repo** (only `scripts/disconnect.sh` touches the markers, and only to strip them), so I corrected it in place — but whatever regenerates it needs the same fix or this reverts on the next run.

## Test

51 files / 661 tests green, plus 13 new in `llm-tier5.test.ts` covering the records, zero-count survival, quoting of a multi-line signature, and the `--detail` gate.

commits.message:
feat(llm): implement --format llm for the five commands that faked it

`explain`, `read`, `status`, `doctor` and `savings` all advertised
`text|json|llm` in their help and rendered `text` when given `llm`.
docs/llm-format.md documented the fallback as intentional — "route to
whichever existing format is most compact" — on the theory that prose and
verbatim source have no record form.

That is true of the payload and false of everything around it. `explain`'s
prose is a rendering of `facts` + `role` + `importance`, so an agent can have
the inputs instead and skip the paragraph entirely; `read`'s source was
arriving under a 4-column line-number gutter and a pair of ANSI escapes per
line. `explain` is the one that mattered: it is the first call most plugins
make on any question, so the fallback was costing the most tokens on the
hottest path.

Measured against `--format json`, which the help text sent agents to as the
workaround: explain -55%, doctor -31%, savings -31%, read -5%, and status
+1%. `read` gains 23% against `text` instead, 601 bytes of which is gutter
and ANSI on a 40-line read.

`status` is kept despite being a wash on size: it is in for the explicit
`stale=true|false` field, which is the question the command gets called to
answer and which `text` only implied through a warning line. Its unreachable
-backend path now emits the spec's `error code=...` record so a consumer
parses the failure the same way it parses a result.

Two exceptions stay on text and are now documented as such: `diff --content`
(verbatim hunks) and `ingest`, a hidden implementation-detail command.

`read`'s content block is the one place the one-record-per-line invariant is
relaxed. The preceding `content lines=<n>` record makes the block
self-delimiting so a line of source can never be mistaken for a record.

Also corrects the CLAUDE.md paragraph on this, which was wrong in both
directions: it claimed `query` advertises `llm` (it offers only `text|json`)
and missed `doctor`, `savings` and `ingest`. It also never mentioned that
seven commands take no `--format` at all, where `--format llm` is an
`unknown option` error rather than a fallback — the one case where an agent
following the "pass it unconditionally" advice breaks.

fix(llm): stop printLlmLines dropping the blank lines read counts

Review follow-up. `read --format llm` frames its payload with
`content lines=<n>` and then prints the raw source, but printLlmLines skipped
falsy entries -- and a blank source line is `""`. So the header counted lines
that never reached stdout, and a consumer honouring the count read the
following records as source.

Wrong on almost every real input, not an edge case: `ix read src/cli/llm.ts
--format llm` declared 91 and emitted 81. Correct only for a file with no
blank lines and no trailing newline.

`!= null` rather than truthiness. printLlmLines had no callers on main before
this branch, so nothing else is affected: every renderer builds lines with a
record kind, and llmLine returns `""` only for a null kind with no surviving
fields, which no caller passes.

The existing test asserted renderReadLlm's return value, which is correct in
isolation -- the defect was in render composed with print. So outputResult is
exported and the new tests drive the real print path across blank lines, an
empty file, CRLF, no trailing newline, and blank-lines-only.

Also pins doctor's status precedence for {ok:true, warn:true} -- the one shape
the ternary ordering decides, and previously uncovered. It renders `ok`, which
is what the glyph line renders for the same record.

Bug restored on both: 6 targeted failures, then byte-exact restore (sha256
verified). tsc/eslint/knip clean, 667 tests pass.

reviews.body:
Two independent review passes (one on your commit, one on my follow-up). Merging.

**The renderers themselves are solid.** Record shape matches the shipped Tier 1–4 convention (header record named after the command, then repeated child records), keys are snake_case throughout with no camelCase leaking, and every field except `read`'s content block goes through `llmLine` → `llmField` → `llmQuote`. Probed the free-text fields directly with embedded newlines, quotes, tabs and backslashes — doctor check names and details, status paths with spaces and quotes, raw-explain docstrings — all correctly escaped, nothing spans two lines. Every docs claim was verified by running the built CLI rather than reading: all seven of `config`/`init`/`reset`/`upgrade`/`view`/`watch`/`docker` do exit 1 with `unknown option`, and `query` really does offer only `text|json`. Three of the strongest test claims mutation-checked and each bites.

**One blocker found and fixed, in a commit I pushed.** `printLlmLines` skipped falsy entries, and a blank source line is `""`. So `read --format llm` counted lines in `content lines=<n>` that never reached stdout, and a consumer honouring the count — the entire point of the self-delimiting block — read the following records as source. Wrong on almost every real input, not an edge case: `ix read src/cli/llm.ts --format llm` declared **91** and emitted **81**. Correct only for a file with no blank lines and no trailing newline.

Changed to `!= null`. Safe because `printLlmLines` had zero callers on `main` before this branch, and I enumerated every path into it: all seven call sites go through renderers that build lines exclusively from `llmLine("<literal>", …)`. The only three `llmLine` calls with a variable kind (`impact.ts:548`, `trace.ts:331`, `format.ts:490`) don't use `printLlmLines`, and the only `push("")` calls are text renderers behind `subsystems`.

Worth naming the trap, because it's the recurring one here: **your test was correct and still passed against the bug.** `expect(lines.slice(2)).toEqual([…, ""])` asserts on `renderReadLlm`'s return value, which was always right — the defect lived in render *composed with* print. So `outputResult` is now exported and the new tests drive the real print path across blank lines, an empty file, CRLF, no-trailing-newline and blank-lines-only.

Also added the `{ok:true, warn:true}` row for `doctor` — the one shape your ternary's ordering actually decides, and previously uncovered. It pins `status=ok`, matching what the glyph line renders for the same record; `warn` would have been wrong. And folded the CLAUDE.md paragraph that still said "these commands take no `--format`" into your new one, since yours is a strict superset (it adds `docker`) and the two contradicted each other two paragraphs apart.

Bug restored on both fixes: 6 targeted failures — 5 framing, 1 doctor. `"no trailing newline"` correctly does *not* fail, since it's the one input the old code got right. tsc/eslint/knip clean, 667 passing.

Not fixed, flagged for follow-up: **the `--format llm` dispatch itself is still untested for all five commands.** Reverting the `"llm"` comparison in each leaves the full suite green. The renderers are covered; the branch that reaches them is not, which is exactly the regression this PR exists to fix. Closing that needs client mocking per command, and I'd rather leave it to you than bolt on a structural test that gives false confidence. Also unfixed: `read`'s not-found and `explain`'s resolve-failure branches still emit human prose to stderr and nothing on stdout, so `ix read bogus --format llm` gives an agent zero bytes and exit 0 — `diff.ts:471` already has the `llmError` precedent.
